claims.kickoff_quote: under the test-driven-development skill — write the failing tests first, then implement to green
claims.skill_quote: Write the test first. Watch it fail. Write minimal code to pass.
claims.reasoning: The em-dash gloss 'write the failing tests first, then implement to green' is a one-line compression of the skill's entire red-green cycle, which SKILL.md states as its Overview (line 10) and again as the Iron Law 'NO PRODUCTION CODE WITHOUT A FAILING TEST FIRST' (line 34) and the Final Rule (lines 367-368). It carries no parameter, no mode selection and no gating the skill cannot supply. It is in fact doubly covered: sprint-execution SKILL.md:132 already binds the same contract ('TDD-first is the default task contract. Every implementation task: write the failing test, watch it fail, implement, watch it pass, commit. Subagents follow the test-driven-development skill; the dispatch prompt says so explicitly'), so the operator restating it a third time adds nothing. Note the gloss is also lossier than the skill — it drops the mandatory 'Verify RED' beat (line 115) and the REFACTOR beat (line 185) — so keeping it is worse than deleting it.

claims.kickoff_quote: Then use the sprint-execution skill to execute PHASE/<NN>-<MM>-PLAN.md under the test-driven-development skill
claims.skill_quote: description: Use when implementing any feature or bugfix, before writing implementation code
claims.reasoning: The composition instruction — that TDD is the discipline sprint-execution executes the named PHASE plan file under — is an argument of the invocation, not methodology. The TDD skill's own trigger (line 3) is generic ('implementing any feature or bugfix') and the skill never names sprint-execution, waves, worktrees or PHASE/<NN>-<MM>-PLAN.md anywhere (grepped 'sprint', 'wave', 'worktree', 'PHASE', 'plan' across SKILL.md and testing-anti-patterns.md — zero hits for the orchestration nouns). Per the ordering/composition rule this is load-bearing and must be KEPT; only the trailing gloss (claim 1) should be cut.
